messages:
Sam: heads-up — customer reports intermittent 502/504s hitting hosted inference when they stream a large multipart request (embeddings + metadata). happens ~20-30% of attempts, looks correlated to big headers.
Elaine: do we have a trace id or curl repro? any sample headers?
Sam: sending sample curl and a short tcpdump snippet.
Sam: ```curl -X POST \ 
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=text-embed-32k' \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundary' \ 
  -H "X-Client-Meta: $(head -c 12000 /dev/urandom | base64)" \ 
  --data-binary @payload.stream```
Sam: quick server-side log around trace xyz-9c3: 
```
2026-03-16T18:02:11.123Z envoy proxy[ld]: [warning] upstream reset: ECONNRESET before response complete; upstream: 10.40.2.12:443, downstream: 10.12.8.45:52344
2026-03-16T18:02:11.124Z nginx frontdoor[pid]: [error] 431 Request Header Fields Too Large: client sent header larger than buffer
```
Elaine: 431 in nginx is a smoking gun. haven't seen a lot of 431s in metrics — deployed a new WAF rule yesterday?
Sasha: I rolled a frontdoor config yesterday that tightened header inspections for WAF signatures. It included a default client_header_buffer_size change (from 4k to 4k) — I didn't touch large_client_header_buffers though.
Ajay: can we repro locally? Sam, what size header triggers it in their test?
Sam: customer used ~12KB x-client-meta. I reproduced with curl above against a staging frontdoor and saw immediate 502 with envoy upstream reset + nginx 431 in the chain.
CliTraceBot: captured full request/response path for trace xyz-9c3: frontend-nginx -> envoy-middle -> midproxy(10.40.2.12) -> model-host. Upstream closed connection when nginx returned 431 to client (proxy behaviour caused 502 to be seen by client).
Sasha: aha — nginx returning 431 to the proxy lead to upstream reset, which our edge translates to 502/504. The customer sees 502/504 while our logs show a 431 earlier.
Elaine: nice find. mitigation options? short-term we can reject with 431 earlier at the edge with a clearer message, long-term bump buffers or sanitize metadata client-side.
Ajay: short-term action: revert the WAF change that tightened header inspection and add an explicit 431 response path so we surface a clear error instead of proxy reset. Also add a routing rule to send large-header flows to a special proxy with larger buffers.
Sasha: config snippet to test on staging: 
```
http {
  large_client_header_buffers 8 16k;
  client_header_buffer_size 4k;
  proxy_buffer_size 32k;
}
```
Sasha: applying to staging now and running the curl repro.
Sam: testing against staging patched config — curl completes with 200 and streaming continues. no envoy upstream reset in logs.
devops-bot: deployment staging/frontdoor-config v2026-03-16_18:20 applied to staging (id: dfb7).
Elaine: next steps — (1) rollback the strict WAF tweak from yesterday into a canary that rejects but returns 431 with human-friendly JSON; (2) schedule a controlled prod roll that increases large_client_header_buffers to 8 16k and proxy_buffer_size to 32k; (3) add metric/alert for 431->502 translation spike; (4) tell customer workaround: shrink X-Client-Meta or switch to hosted metadata store (we provide a signed meta pointer).
Ajay: I'll own the prod rollout window and run a perf sweep to ensure memory/buffer changes don't regress frontdoor throughput.
Sasha: I'll add a sentinel check in the WAF rule to not escalate header-trim to connection reset (ensure nginx returns 431 to client, not upstream).
Sam: I'll message the customer with repro findings + immediate workaround and ETA for patch.
Elaine: also file a follow-up to devdocs — document header limits for hosted API and recommended metadata encoding.
Sam: thanks team — keeping thread open until prod patch is verified.
Ajay: PROD rollout scheduled 2026-03-17 02:00 UTC, will post results here.
Sam: noted. closing for now but will update when prod looks green.
